chapter: Road shows, carnivals and New York
title: Carnival and road-show employers until returning to New Orleans in 1956
summary: Punch runs through Bronze Mannequins, Jerry Jackson's Cavaliers, Royal American, Silas Green and Jimmy Straits before coming home late 1956.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I see. So, you went, after New York you went on with these carnivals.
Yeah, I went back on the road.
And first were the Bronze Mannequins, and then when? And then who were some of the others?

Well, now I'm going to tell you, the Bronze Mannequins, this year he played the Heaney Brothers. And they shared he had two calls, he put one band over on the Heaney Brothers and one band on James C. Straits. Well I'd manage this band, some other fellow managed that band. Well I still would try to tell you about four years, but he sent for his brother and gave his brother a show, and he was such a wild catcher, you know, couldn't nobody get along with him, so I just quit my whole outfit. After about three or four years I'd been with him, see. Then I joined a man called Jerry Jackson, from Nashville, Tennessee. He played the Cavaliers show. I worked with him about a couple years.
He didn't play, he just do the booking and manage the show and things.
Any New Orleans guys in those bands?

No. Then I went with this show called The Royal American, that's the biggest show on the road, I played with them three years. I left them and went to Silas Green and played with him two and a half years, after that, see. When I left Silas Green, well, I went to Jimmy Straits with a fellow named Scotty, a great drummer, that's when I left him and come on to New Orleans in 56. Got Scott taking him, he was getting sick, he wanted me to stay up there, but I stole it off from him. The fellow was leaving, coming to Memphis in his car, and I just got in the car and come on to Memphis, and him from Memphis I grabbed the train and come on to New Orleans, I've been there ever since.
When did you get here, what year?
